source_documents.title: Intermolecular Interactions in Crystals Modulate Intramolecular Excited State Proton Transfer Reactions

conditions_studied: crystal: single crystals (fs transient absorption, absorption, fluorescence)

reference_evidence_units.quote: These isomers show intermolecular hydrogen bonding within the crystal lattice, resulting in larger excitonic couplings, which significantly alters their reaction pathways compared to their behavior in solution.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1,4- and 1,5-DHAQ
reference_evidence_units.statement: Intermolecular H-bonds in the crystal raise excitonic coupling and change the excited-state pathway.

reference_evidence_units.quote: We show that 1,8-DHAQ, which does not form intermolecular hydrogen bonds in the crystal, shows minimal changes in dynamics between the phases.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1,8-DHAQ
reference_evidence_units.statement: Without intermolecular H-bonds the ESIPT dynamics barely change.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In contrast, in the case of 1,4-DHAQ, intermolecular interactions within the molecular crystal phase open up an ESIPT relaxation channel, which is not observed in the solution phase.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1,4-DHAQ
reference_evidence_units.statement: An ESIPT channel appears only in the crystal.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The fitted time constants for 1,8-DHAQ crystals suggest analogous assignments; subpicosecond time scales for proton transfer, vibrational relaxation occurring over tens of picoseconds, and an electronic state lifetime extending several hundred picoseconds.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1,8-DHAQ
reference_evidence_units.statement: Sub-ps proton transfer in the crystal, as in solution.

reference_evidence_units.quote: only the subps component has physical significance, likely corresponding to the ESIPT process in 1,5DHAQ, as previously confirmed by time-resolved fluorescence studies on microcrystals.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1,5-DHAQ
reference_evidence_units.statement: Sub-ps component assigned to ESIPT; fast nonradiative decay in the crystal.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Molecular orbitals (MOs) from TDDFT calculations, using an eight-molecule-in-lattice model, reveal more delocalized excitation, or exciton character, in the crystalline phase compared to the solution-phase transitions (Figures S8− S11).
reference_evidence_units.subject: DHAQ crystals
reference_evidence_units.statement: Excitations delocalise over neighbours in the crystal.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In contrast, the absorption line of 1,8DHAQ crystals exhibited a Gaussian profile, similar to its solution phase, implying that the excitonic effects are less pronounced as found theoretically (Table 1).
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1,8-DHAQ
reference_evidence_units.statement: No excitonic splitting in the 1,8 crystal.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The splitting indicates that the two absorption bands near the edge of the spectrum are associated with excitonic states.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1,4-/1,5-DHAQ
reference_evidence_units.statement: Split band edge assigned to excitonic states.

reference_evidence_units.quote: ESIPT is predicted to be slightly exothermic in 1,4-DHAQ (Figure 5(b)) with an energy gap of 0.09 eV, whereas there is a strong driving force for the occurrence of ESIPT in 1,8-DHAQ and in 1,5-DHAQ (Figures S14 and S17).
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1,4-, 1,5-, 1,8-DHAQ
reference_evidence_units.statement: Weak ESIPT driving force in 1,4-DHAQ, strong in 1,8 and 1,5.

reference_evidence_units.quote: a remarkable change for the molecular dynamics of 1,4-DHAQ between solution and crystal, indicating the generation of a fast nonradiative pathway, i.e., ESIPT, in the presence of the solid-state lattice for the bath coupling.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1,4-DHAQ
reference_evidence_units.statement: The lattice opens fast ESIPT-mediated nonradiative decay.

contrast_group.varied_factor: position of the two hydroxy groups on anthraquinone (1,8 vs 1,5 vs 1,4)
contrast_group.paper_difference: 1,8-DHAQ has no intermolecular H-bonds in the crystal and its ESIPT dynamics are unchanged; in 1,5- and 1,4-DHAQ intermolecular H-bonds and excitonic coupling change the pathway, and in 1,4-DHAQ ESIPT opens only in the crystal.
